objective_for_doctor: A 27-year-old F patient presents to the clinic. Chief complaint: nasal congestion.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?
I have nasal congestion, a cough with colored or more abundant sputum than usual, a sore throat, fever, and diffuse muscle pain.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—how long have these symptoms been going on, and do you have any shortness of breath or chest pain?  
Doctor: Also, is your fever measured (how high), and have you had known sick contacts or tested positive for COVID/flu recently?

Doctor: Okay—does your sore throat feel mainly scratchy vs severe, and are you having any runny nose or sneezing? Also, have you noticed wheezing, or are you short of breath when walking up stairs?  
Doctor: And on a scale of 0–10, how bad is the fever/chills and the muscle pain?

Doctor: I’ll examine you now—please tell me if you have wheezing and whether your cough is worse at night.  
Doctor: Also, any history of asthma, pregnancy, or smoking, and do you feel short of breath right now?

Yes—I'm a cigarette smoker, and I’m exposed to secondhand cigarette smoke daily. I don’t know whether I have wheezing, and I don’t know if my cough is worse at night. I don’t know if I feel short of breath right now.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—thanks; I’ll check your vitals and lungs now: do you have a thermometer reading, oxygen saturation if available, and can you tell me if your cough is productive (what color) and whether you have sinus/facial pressure?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Rapid_COVID_Flu_Antigen_or_PCR; REQUEST TEST: CBC_with_Differential; REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray.

I don’t know. My cough is productive with colored or more abundant sputum than usual. I also have nasal congestion, and I have pain in relation to my reason for consulting, including pain at the top of the head and the right cheek.

Doctor: I’m Dr. Agent—on my lung exam, do you notice any wheeze or crackles (or do you feel breathless when speaking), and do you have facial/sinus tenderness on the right cheek?  
Doctor: Do you have any severe headache with neck stiffness, rash, or eye pain/vision changes—yes or no?  
Doctor: REQUEST TEST: Vital_Signs_with_SpO2_and_Temperature; REQUEST TEST: Sinus_assessment (transillumination/TTP); once results are back I’ll decide.

Doctor: Thanks—if you have no neck stiffness/rash/eye pain/vision changes and your lung exam shows no wheeze/crackles (or you’re not significantly breathless), then the top-right cheek/facial tenderness plus fever, myalgias, sore throat, and productive colored sputum most fits an acute viral respiratory infection with likely acute bacterial rhinosinusitis.  
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute rhinosinusitis (most consistent with acute bacterial rhinosinusitis) likely following an acute viral URI
